name: Hispanic
recordTerm: not recorded separately; counted as Caucasian
note: The record did not keep a Hispanic category, so the count is an estimate (about 3,000–3,500, or 5–6% of deaths, against about 4.5% of the population). Ralph Guzmán’s 1969 study of the Southwest found Spanish-surnamed men were 19% of the region’s casualties and about 12% of its population.
source: Defense Casualty Analysis System (DCAS), Vietnam Conflict Extract File, race field; US Census 1970; Guzmán 1969; Appy, Working-Class War (1993).
